title: Unit – 5 : Session – 2 : SLO – 1  |  Graph Representation — Adjacency Matrix
sections: In an adjacency matrix for a graph with n vertices, the size of the matrix is n x n.
If there is an edge between vertex i and vertex j, then adjacency_matrix[i][j] = 1.
In an undirected graph, the adjacency matrix is always SYMMETRIC.
In a directed graph, adjacency_matrix[i][j] = 1 means there is a directed edge from i to j.
The space complexity of an adjacency matrix representation is O(n^2).
The adjacency matrix is suitable for representing sparse graphs — FALSE (it wastes space; lists suit sparse graphs).
In a weighted graph, adjacency matrix elements can store the weight values instead of 1s and 0s — TRUE.
In an undirected graph, adjacency_matrix[i][j] will always equal adjacency_matrix[j][i] — TRUE.
Adjacency matrices use less memory compared to adjacency lists for dense graphs — TRUE.
Adjacency matrix: a 2-D n x n array where entry [i][j] is 1 (or the edge weight) if an edge exists between
vertex i and vertex j, and 0 otherwise.
Advantages: (1) edge existence checked in O(1) time; (2) simple to implement and easy to store weights.
